speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to help me understand the cause, how long has this lesion been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The patient's history of Crohn's disease and uveitis, combined with a painful ulcer that appeared at the site of a minor trauma (ant bite) and has progressed over one month, is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum, a neutrophilic dermatosis. This diagnosis is further supported by her history of diabetes and steroid use, which can influence the presentation.
